claims.claim: Ottawa listed the $5.9-billion Roberts Bank Terminal 2 expansion as a project of national interest, which the Surrey Now-Leader says can move commercial operations to 2035 rather than 2039.
claims.episode_span: accelerate commercial operations by up to four years, to 2035 rather than 2039
claims.source_title: $5.9B Delta container port expansion of ‘national interest’: Canadian government
claims.supporting_quote: The federal government says declaring RBT2 a project of national interest accelerates the project’s commercial operations by up to four years — meaning it will be ready to operate by 2035 rather than 2039.

claims.claim: The expansion is expected to add 2.4 million containers of capacity at the Port of Vancouver.
claims.episode_span: expected to add 2.4 million containers of capacity
claims.source_title: Ottawa lists Roberts Bank port expansion in B.C. as project of national interest
claims.supporting_quote: The planned Roberts Bank Terminal 2 expansion, which is expected to add 2.4 million containers of capacity at the Port of Vancouver, the largest in the country, has officially been named a project of national interest.

claims.claim: Steven MacKinnon announced the listing on Friday, October 30, at the Delta port with Jill McKnight, Lorne Doerkson, Laura Cassidy, and Peter Xotta.
claims.episode_span: Transport Minister Steven MacKinnon announced the listing Friday, October 30, at the Delta port
claims.source_title: $5.9B Delta container port expansion of ‘national interest’: Canadian government
claims.supporting_quote: Minister of Transport Steven MacKinnon was on hand to make the announcement, alongside Delta MP Jill McKnight, B.C. premier-designate Lorne Doerkson, Tsawwassen First Nation Chief Laura Cassidy, Vancouver Fraser Port Authority president and CEO Peter Xotta, and other political and business leaders.

claims.claim: MacKinnon said the Port of Vancouver connects businesses to more than 170 markets and handles about one-third of Canada's trade outside the United States.
claims.episode_span: connects Canadian businesses to more than 170 markets and handles about one-third of Canada's trade outside the United States
claims.source_title: $5.9B Delta container port expansion of ‘national interest’: Canadian government
claims.supporting_quote: The minister noted the Port of Vancouver is Canada’s largest port “by a long margin,” connecting Canadian businesses to more than 170 markets around the world and handling approximately one-third of Canada’s trade outside the United States.

claims.claim: Mark Carney said listing the terminal better connects the economy with the world and that Canada will not wait.
claims.episode_span: Carney said in a statement that the listing better connects the economy with the world and diversifies trade
claims.source_title: $5.9B Delta container port expansion of ‘national interest’: Canadian government
claims.supporting_quote: “By listing Roberts Bank Terminal 2 as a project of national interest, we are better connecting our economy with the world and diversifying our trade,” Prime Minister Mark Carney said in a statement.

claims.claim: The designation lets the project bypass remaining federal permits, with a conditions document from Dominic Leblanc that officials said can be ready within a couple of months.
claims.episode_span: a conditions document will be issued by the minister responsible under the act, currently Internal Trade Minister Dominic Leblanc
claims.source_title: $5.9B Delta container port expansion of ‘national interest’: Canadian government
claims.supporting_quote: That conditions document can be ready within “a couple of months,” according to senior government officials in a technical briefing with media.

claims.claim: The port authority committed to 102 hectares of fish habitat offsetting and proposed measures including underwater noise mitigation for southern resident killer whales and chinook salmon.
claims.episode_span: committed to 102 hectares of fish-habitat offsetting
claims.source_title: $5.9B Delta container port expansion of ‘national interest’: Canadian government
claims.supporting_quote: The Port Authority has also committed to 102 hectares of fish habitat offsetting.

claims.claim: Chief Laura Cassidy said Tsawwassen First Nation support is not unconditional and that concerns remain about the Fraser River estuary and the Salish Sea.
claims.episode_span: Chief Laura Cassidy said Tsawwassen First Nation's support is not unconditional
claims.source_title: $5.9B Delta container port expansion of ‘national interest’: Canadian government
claims.supporting_quote: Speaking at Friday’s announcement, Tsawwassen First Nation Chief Laura Cassidy said environmental protections are key to TFN’s consent to the project, noting their support is not unconditional.
